title: Apple's First AI Glasses Planned to Debut at WWDC 2027, Launch by Year-End

content_html:
According to tech blogger Mark Gurman, Apple plans to unveil its first AI smart glasses at the WWDC Worldwide Developers Conference in June 2027, with an official launch expected by the end of 2027. The product’s internal codename is N50, and its hardware design is now largely finalized.

In terms of appearance, Apple’s AI glasses are overall slimmer than Meta’s second-generation Ray-Ban smart glasses, with the camera integrated directly into the frame and no noticeable bump. Apple has also prepared multiple styles and color options, with a focus on optimizing sound quality, sensor configuration, and wearing comfort.

Functionally, the first-generation product will not use the display approach of traditional AR glasses. Instead, it will center its interaction around the AI voice assistant Siri, using the camera to perceive the surrounding environment and support features such as building recognition, real-time translation, and navigation guidance. Users can also use voice commands to have Siri identify ingredients in the refrigerator and recommend recipes, or directly handle tasks such as restaurant reservations, ride-hailing calls, and purchases of coffee and movie tickets, reducing dependence on the iPhone.

From a product positioning perspective, Apple is trying to integrate an AI assistant, environmental perception, and everyday life services into a lightweight wearable device, exploring an AI glasses interaction format that differs from traditional AR display devices.
